Area Forecast Discussion...UPDATED
National Weather Service San Diego CA
410 AM PST Wed Nov 18 2026

.SYNOPSIS...
Cool weather will continue for the next week. Rain, isolated 
thunderstorms, high mountain snow, and stronger winds are 
expected Thursday into Thursday night as a storm system moves
through California. Dry but cool weather will follow Friday 
through Sunday. The next system looks weaker and could bring 
light rain Sunday night and Monday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...FOR EXTREME SOUTHWESTERN CALIFORNIA INCLUDING ORANGE...
SAN DIEGO...WESTERN RIVERSIDE AND SOUTHWESTERN SAN BERNARDINO
COUNTIES...

Mostly clear skies continue overhead, and with fairly calm winds,
temperatures are on the chilly side this morning. At 2 AM, most 
inland valleys were in the 40s, with a few spots in the upper 
30s, and mountain valleys in the 20s. Today will be fair but cool
after the chilly start, with highs in the mid 60s to lower 70s for
lower elevations. That's about 4-10 degrees below average for 
valleys, and about 1-3 degrees below average at the coast. The 
next storm Thursday will be pretty strong, with a well-defined 
front moving through SoCal. Rain should begin in the L.A. Basin 
Thursday morning, moving southeast into Riverside and San Diego 
Counties through the afternoon. Rain will be pretty intense along 
the front, and there is a small chance of thunderstorms. For both 
reasons, rainfall rates could reach 0.50-0.65 per hour, which 
could produce some urban flooding. Snow levels will start out 
high, and drop to about 6,500 feet by the time the precipitation 
moves out. A few inches should accumulate above 7,500 feet, on the
upper ski slopes around Big Bear. Down at Big Bear Lake, little 
if any accumulations are expected. But the timing of the cold air 
moving in with the moisture are uncertain, so there's a range of 
potential snowfall outcomes. Winds will be strongest ahead of and 
along the front, with gusts exceeding 25-30 mph for the coast and 
40-55 mph in the mountains and adjacent desert slopes, where 
there's a wind advisory. Showers will follow the front Thursday 
evening as the snow level lowers, but then will eventually end 
Thursday night. Friday will start out quite cold, but clouds will 
clear to bring mostly sunny conditions. A secondary shortwave 
rotates through the Great Basin Friday, but for now it doesn't 
appear to prolong the precipitation, just postpone any warm up. A 
touch of offshore flow pays a visit Friday night and Saturday, but
any brisk offshore winds will be quite isolated in foothills. 
High pressure aloft doesn't build much, but enough to provide dry 
and slightly warmer weather Friday through the weekend. 
Temperatures will continue below normal each of those days, with 
highs in the mid 60s to lower 70s at lower elevations, upper 30s 
to mid 50s in the mountains, and 50s in the High Desert. Model 
guidance is starting to narrow the possibilities regarding the 
timing of the next precipitation. A weak shortwave moves into the 
region Sunday, bringing light showers Sunday night and Monday. 
Right now this system looks much weaker regarding precipitation 
amounts and winds. By Tuesday there's some guidance showing a 
continuation of the unsettled, occasionally wet and windy pattern.
But there are nearly equal numbers of ensemble members showing a 
stronger ridge pattern for dry and warmer weather heading into the
holiday.
&&

.AVIATION... 
181200Z...Coast/Valleys...SCT clouds with bases around 3000-4000 ft 
MSL, with low clouds going BKN (20-30%) intermittently (mainly from 
thru 15z Wed) along the coastal areas. Otherwise, SCT-BKN high 
clouds will build into the region Wednesday morning. Clouds will 
begin to lift a little and regather again, mainly after 06z Thu as 
another low pressure system begins to approach the region. Low 
clouds will continue to increase and thicken going into the early 
morning hours tomorrow, near the end of the forecast period. There 
is a very isolated chance (less than 10 percent) of -SHRA tomorrow 
morning at the coastal sites, although the onset of precipitation is 
not expected to begin until after 18z Thursday.

Mountains/Deserts...VFR conditions will prevail with clouds 4000-
6000 ft along coastal slopes scattering early in the morning. SCT-
BKN AOA 15k feet MSL mid-high level clouds will build into the 
region Wednesday morning and throughout the rest of the forecast 
period.

&&

.MARINE...
A Small Craft Advisory has been issued for 12z Thursday through 18z 
Friday, as conditions look to deteriorate once again on Thursday as 
the next storm system approaches. Steep, high seas of 7-10 ft, along 
with wind gusts peaking 20-30 knots, are expected for Thursday into 
Friday morning. Wind direction initially south-southwest on Thursday 
will turn westerly by late afternoon and continue through early 
morning on Friday. Conditions will begin to improve by later in the 
day on Friday with much calmer seas expected by the weekend.

&&

.BEACHES...
The shorter period northwest swell will wane through this evening, 
leaving a 3-5 ft swell with a 13-14 second period for today. This 
will result in a brief decrease in surf, down to 3-5 feet. However, 
northwesterly swell builds again tomorrow, elevating surf once again 
by later in the evening and into early Friday.

Coastal flooding is expected at times through the rest of the week. 
King Tides are expected to peak next week, but chances of tides 
exceeding 7 ft start as early as Saturday Nov 21.

&&

.SKYWARN... 
Skywarn activation is not requested. However weather spotters are
encouraged to report significant weather conditions.
